requirement:
The Rust outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Functions, methods, and function signatures | `fn` | Declared name |
| Structs, enums, unions, and traits | `struct`, `enum`, `union`, `trait` | Declared name |
| Implementations | `impl` | Written self type and optional trait path |
| Modules | `mod` | Declared name |
| Macro definitions | `macro` | Declared name |
| Macro invocations in item position | `macro` | Anonymous |
| Constants and statics | `const`, `static` | Declared name |
| Type aliases and associated types | `type` | Declared name |
| Foreign blocks | `extern` | ABI string, or `Rust` when absent |
| Extern-crate declarations | `extern-crate` | Declared name |
| Imports | `use` | Anonymous |

An implementation of `Trait` for `Thing` uses `impl[Thing/Trait]`;
an inherent implementation uses `impl[Thing]`. Nesting follows source
containment within the file. Outer attributes and outer documentation comments
attach to the following item; inner documentation comments belong to their
containing item or file root.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
I judged the tests against each clause of `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.items`. I found no gap. I did not request implementation source.

**Item kinds, kind names and name rules**
- Functions, methods and signatures:
  - Nested and method functions are covered in `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` (`crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs`): `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`, `impl[Thing]/fn[run]` and `mod[local]/fn[run]`.
  - Signatures without a body are covered by `trait[Trait]/fn[read]` and `extern[C]/fn[puts]`.
- Structs, enums, unions and traits: `struct[Thing]`, `union[U]`, `enum[E]` and `trait[Trait]` are asserted in the same test.
- Implementations:
  - `impl[Thing]` covers an inherent implementation.
  - `impl[Thing/Trait]` covers a trait implementation.
  - `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]` covers a written self type.
  - `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` is asserted in `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not`.
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` (`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs`) asserts `impl[Thing/core::fmt::Display]` for a qualified trait path.
  - `rust_name_spans_highlight_spelling_in_the_original_source` checks the name spans.
- Modules: `mod[local]` is an inline module and `mod[external]` is a declaration without a body.
- Macro definitions: `macro[make]` is asserted.
- Macro invocations:
  - `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` checks that item-position macros get `macro@<12 hex>` selectors, at file level, in an impl and in a mod.
  - The same test asserts that expression macros inside a function body create no nodes, via `selectors.len() == 7`.
- Constants and statics: `const[C]` and `static[S]`.
- Type aliases and associated types: `type[Alias]` and `trait[Trait]/type[Item]`.
- Foreign blocks: `extern[C]` for an explicit ABI. `extern[Rust]` for an absent ABI is asserted in two tests. One of them also covers `unsafe extern`.
- Extern-crate declarations: `extern-crate[core]`.
- Imports: `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` and `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` assert that `use` selectors start with `use@` and that the two imports differ. The first also checks identity-hash stability and `#1`/`#2` suffixes for duplicate imports.
- Kind strings are asserted exactly in `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes`: `["","mod","fn","struct","fn"]`.

**Nesting follows source containment**
- Full selector lists are asserted exactly, for example `mod[auth]/fn[check]` and `mod[auth]/struct[Token]`.
- Nesting inside a function body is covered by `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`.

**Attachment of attributes and comments**
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` checks that an outer doc comment and `#[inline]` attach to the following item. The selected text starts with `/// Check tokens.`, contains `#[inline]`, and the span start equals the position of the doc comment.
- `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` and `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` cover inner documentation:
  - Inner `//!` and `/*! */` comments at file level belong to the root.
  - `//! Module docs.` belongs to `mod[m]`.
  - Preceding comment runs belong to the next node, and line ranges are asserted.

**Selector grammar, percent encoding, anonymous identities and duplicate suffixes**
- The requirement delegates these to `requirements.references.outline_selectors`, which is cited context and not reassessed here.
- The subject's cases are still exercised: percent encoding of `[u8; 4]`, `#1`/`#2` suffixes on duplicate `repeated`, and a resolve error for the ambiguous `fn[repeated]`.

All the tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so I found no marking gap.
